trial_court: Court of learned Senior Civil Judge, Patiala House Court (Ct. No. 1504/2018)
case_name: Vipul Kant Upadhyay vs Standard Chartered Bank
facts_of_case: Complaint case under Section 25 of the Payment & Settlement Systems Act, 2007 pending in the trial court; petitioner seeks quashing of complaint and stay of further proceedings.

legal_principles.principle: A person cannot be a party to a criminal complaint if they have ceased to be a director of the accused company.
legal_principles.held: Hence, he cannot be a party to the criminal complaint under Section 25 of Payment & Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
use_in: divorce cases where directorship is involved

legal_principles.principle: A bounced ECS cannot be the basis for a criminal complaint.
legal_principles.held: It is stated by Mr Chaudhary, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner that the complaint under Section 25 of the Payment & Settlement Systems Act, 2007 is misconceived as in the present case, the ECS bounced on 01.12.2017 whereas the petitioner has ceased to be a Director of M/s. IAP. Company Pvt. Ltd. i.e. accused No. 1 on 18.10.2017.

outcome.result: Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions
outcome.final_order: Proceedings in case being Ct. No. 1504/2018 shall remain stayed till the next hearing; issue notice to respondent by all modes including electronic on the petitioner taking requisite steps within one week from today.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for quashing a complaint case
seeking stay of further proceedings in a criminal complaint
using Section 25 of the Payment & Settlement Systems Act
